'''PyMC''' (formerly known as PyMC3) is a [[probabilistic programming]] library for [[Python (programming language)|Python]]. It can be used for Bayesian statistical modeling and probabilistic machine learning.

PyMC performs inference based on advanced Markov chain Monte Carlo and/or variational fitting algorithms.<ref>Abril-Pla O, Andreani V, Carroll C, Dong L, Fonnesbeck CJ, Kochurov M, Kumar R, Lao J, Luhmann CC, Martin OA, Osthege M, Vieira R, Wiecki T, Zinkov R. (2023) PyMC: a modern, and comprehensive probabilistic programming framework in Python. PeerJ Comput. Sci. 9:e1516 {{doi|10.7717/peerj-cs.1516|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Martin2024">{{cite book|url=https://bap.com.ar|title=Bayesian Analysis with Python|last1=Martin|first1=Osvaldo|date=2024|publisher=Packt Publishing Ltd|isbn=978-1-80512-716-1|language=en|access-date=24 February 2024}}</ref><ref name="Martin2021">{{cite book|url=https://www.routledge.com/Bayesian-Modeling-and-Computation-in-Python/Martin-Kumar-Lao/p/book/9780367894368|title=Bayesian Modeling and Computation in Python|last1=Martin|first1=Osvaldo|last2=Kumar|first2=Ravin|last3=Lao|first3=Junpeng|date=2021|publisher=CRC-press|isbn=978-0-367-89436-8|pages=1–420|language=en|access-date=7 July 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rMKiCgAAQBAJ|title=Bayesian Methods for Hackers: Probabilistic Programming and Bayesian Inference|last=Davidson-Pilon|first=Cameron|date=2015-09-30|publisher=Addison-Wesley Professional|isbn=978-0-13-390292-1|language=en}}</ref>
It is a rewrite from scratch of the previous version of the PyMC software.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://docs.pymc.io|title=documentation |language=en|access-date=2017-09-20}}</ref>
Unlike PyMC2, which had used [[Fortran]] extensions for performing computations, PyMC relies on PyTensor, a Python library that allows defining, optimizing, and efficiently evaluating mathematical expressions involving multi-dimensional arrays.
From version 3.8 PyMC relies on [[ArviZ]] to handle plotting, diagnostics, and statistical checks. PyMC and [[Stan (software)|Stan]] are the two most popular [[probabilistic programming]] tools.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blog.fastforwardlabs.com/2017/01/30/the-algorithms-behind-probabilistic-programming.html|title=The Algorithms Behind Probabilistic Programming|access-date=2017-03-10}}</ref>
PyMC is an [[Open-source software|open source]] project, developed by the community and has been fiscally sponsored by [[NumFOCUS]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.numfocus.org/blog/numfocus-announces-new-fiscally-sponsored-project-pymc3|title=NumFOCUS Announces New Fiscally Sponsored Project: PyMC3|work=NumFOCUS {{!}} Open Code = Better Science|access-date=2017-03-10}}</ref>

After [[Theano (software)|Theano]] announced plans to discontinue development in 2017,<ref>{{cite mailing list|url=https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/theano-users/7Poq8BZutbY|title=MILA and the future of Theano|date=28 September 2017|mailing-list=theano-users|last=Lamblin|first=Pascal|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref> the PyMC team evaluated [[TensorFlow|TensorFlow Probability]] as a computational backend,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://medium.com/@pymc_devs/theano-tensorflow-and-the-future-of-pymc-6c9987bb19d5|title=Theano, TensorFlow and the Future of PyMC|last=Developers|first=PyMC|date=2018-05-17|website=PyMC Developers|access-date=2019-01-25}}</ref> but decided in 2020 to [[Fork (software development)|fork]] Theano under the name Aesara.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Future of PyMC3, or: Theano is Dead, Long Live Theano |url=https://pymc-devs.medium.com/the-future-of-pymc3-or-theano-is-dead-long-live-theano-d8005f8a0e9b |website=PyMC Developers |date=27 October 2020 |access-date=10 January 2021}}</ref>
Large parts of the Theano codebase have been refactored and compilation through [[Google JAX|JAX]]<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bradbury |first1=James |last2=Frostig |first2=Roy |last3=Hawkins |first3=Peter |last4=James |first4=Matthew James |last5=Leary |first5=Chris |last6=Maclaurin |first6=Dougal |last7=Necula |first7=George |last8=Paszke |first8=Adam |last9=VanderPlas |first9=Jake |last10=Wanderman-Milne |first10=Skye |last11=Zhang |first11=Qiao |title=JAX |website=[[GitHub]] |url=https://github.com/google/jax |access-date=10 January 2021}}</ref> and [[Numba]] were added.
The PyMC team has released the revised computational backend under the name PyTensor and continues the development of PyMC.<ref>{{cite web |title=PyMC Timeline |url=https://github.com/pymc-devs/pymc3/wiki/Timeline |website=PyMC Timeline |access-date=10 January 2021}}</ref>

== Inference engines ==
PyMC implements non-gradient-based and gradient-based [[Markov chain Monte Carlo]] (MCMC) algorithms for Bayesian inference and stochastic, gradient-based [[variational Bayesian methods]] for approximate Bayesian inference.
* MCMC-based algorithms:
** No-U-Turn sampler<ref name="NUTS2014">{{cite journal
 | last1 = Hoffman | first1 = Matthew D.
 | last2 = Gelman |first2 = Andrew
 | title = The No-U-Turn Sampler: Adaptively Setting Path Lengths in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
 | journal = [[Journal of Machine Learning Research]]
 |date=April 2014
 | volume = 15
 | pages = ''pp.'' 1593&ndash;1623
 | url = http://jmlr.org/papers/v15/hoffman14a.html
}}</ref> (NUTS), a variant of [[Hybrid Monte Carlo|Hamiltonian Monte Carlo]] and PyMC's default engine for continuous variables
** [[Metropolis–Hastings algorithm|Metropolis–Hastings]], PyMC's default engine for discrete variables
** Sequential Monte Carlo for static posteriors
** Sequential Monte Carlo for [[approximate Bayesian computation]]  
* [[Variational inference]] algorithms:
** Black-box Variational Inference<ref name="kucukelbir20153">{{cite journal
 |last1 = Kucukelbir|first1 = Alp|last2 = Ranganath|first2 = Rajesh|last3 = Blei|first3 = David M.|title = Automatic Variational Inference in Stan|date = June 2015|volume = 1506|issue = 3431|arxiv = 1506.03431|bibcode = 2015arXiv150603431K}}</ref>
